narrative:
On September 22, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 42.6%, hearing 1,270 of the 2,982 scheduled matters across 49 benches. This performance represents an increase from the previous day's rate of 39.5% (1,279 heard of 3,238 scheduled) and marginally exceeds clearance levels recorded on September 18 (42.0%) and September 17 (41.5%).

Bench-level output displayed substantial variation across the court halls. Justice K.S. Hemalekha in Hall 28 posted the highest individual hearing efficiency, addressing 29 of 30 scheduled cases (96.7%). Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde maintained strong momentum, taking up 41 of 51 matters (80.4%) in his primary roster after recording 80.9% on September 21. High aggregate volumes were processed by Justice C.M. Poonacha, who heard 133 cases across two rosters, and Justice M. Nagaprasanna, who heard 64 of 112 cases (57.1%). Conversely, complete non-clearance occurred in Hall 1 under the Chief Justice and Justice K.S. Hemalekha (0 of 38), Hall 7 under Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad (0 of 150), and Hall 35 under Justice Geetha K.B. (0 of 85).

Early-stage proceedings accounted for the bulk of court business. The Orders stage achieved a 52.8% conversion rate (479 heard of 908), marking an increase from 45.9% yesterday. Cases listed for Admission achieved a 45.1% hearing rate (360 of 799), consistent with the 45.3% reported on September 21. Substantive stages progressed more slowly: Final Hearings cleared 24.0% (135 of 562), down from 27.7% on the prior day, while Further Hearings reached only 15.5%. 

Writ Petitions constituted the largest category, comprising 1,297 listings and converting at 42.4% (550 heard), which reflected an increase over the 34.9% seen previously. Criminal Petitions remained steady at 52.4% (268 of 511), whereas Criminal Revision Petitions saw negligible movement, hearing only 2 of 88 matters (2.3%).
